about: Shared test vectors of the review rules (README.md, "Review rules"). The Python tests (review_glob.test.py, review_judge.test.py) read this file, and the TypeScript side reads the same file: a change to the matching or the judge that updates one side only fails the other side's tests. Paths are made up. `globs`: [glob, path, matches]. `cases`: a config from `configs` (a whole `review` block, which must parse), the changed paths as `git diff --name-status -M` prints them ([status, path] or [R<score>|C<score>, old, new]), and the expected weight, required lenses (in order), rules hit (in rule order) and protected paths (in diff order). The config file is `config_path`. `findings`: a lens report body and what review_judge.read_findings reads in it ([kind, line] of each blocker or major, and whether it has a findings section); `group` says which rule it shows. `scans`: counted posts (by the lens author association, in order, one second apart, `edited` and `hidden` as GitHub records them) and what lens.Review.lens_scan reads with `override_prefix` (the history of [name, sha] and each lens key's newest [sha, why]; a lens report, one with the lens marker, that is not one valid read is a `comment without a first-line lens header` entry that reads nothing, and so is a post without the marker that looks like a report and holds an open finding (a blocker or major, or NOT SAFE, as review_judge.read_findings reads it); `not_lens`, when there is one: [where, why] of each post that looks like a report but has no lens marker, so is no lens report, as lens.Review.not_lens_reports names them). `rounds`: review_judge.judge_rounds on a history, each lens key's newest entry [how, body], `decided`, and `changes` (sha -> what the pull request changes at it; a sha not listed is its own change). `reads`: posts as in `scans` (each by its `author`, else `someone`; an override comment is `<override_prefix> <sha>: ...`), the `head`, the reads that are its change merged with the base (`same`) and `override_authors`, under the `basic` rules in enforce with findings judged: lens.Review.lens_reads (each lens key's sha), the keys head_check.review_rounds fails until that lens posts again (`again`: UNREAD, or a report with no findings section) and whether head_check.verdict with the `required` lenses and the rounds pass (`passes`); T3's lens_start reads the same (lensStart.ts), and its vectors hold no finding in a report that counts and stay under the round cap. `unicode`: `refused` is what T3 refuses on a runtime that assigns those code points (a letter, number, mark, format character or space there): a new symbol reads alike on both sides. Every section is run by both sides: a test fails if one side meets a section or a vector it does not run. How a vector is made: README.md, "Review rules".
